key_insight: Topological and graph-based features extracted from ATP player networks can predict tennis match outcomes above chance, even without rankings.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that persistent-homology summaries and temporal graph similarity can add predictive value to sports analytics pipelines when classical ranking features are missing or incomplete.
method: Lower-star filtration on player competitive networks with persistent homology summaries (VAB, HNAV, HWNAV, OW-HNPV) plus Modified Band Depth.
Graph-theoretic features and a modified Katz similarity index with temporal edge weighting.
Random Forest models combining topology, centrality, and ranking signals; topology-only and held-out comparisons.
evidence_signal: Using about 66,000 ATP singles matches from 2000–2025, the main Random Forest model reached 66.2% accuracy (AUC 0.719), while the topology-only model still achieved 63.56% accuracy and the modified Katz approach reached 62.48% on held-out data.
watch_item: The topology pipeline relies on approximations such as ego-graph reduction and triangle elimination, so results may depend on these preprocessing choices and may be sensitive to match-network construction.
paper_title: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction
